subject: physics
question_text: A girl is swinging while seated in a swing. What is the effect on the frequency of oscillation if she stands up?

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The length changes
lines: A swing is a simple pendulum whose length is
measured down to the centre of mass of the
girl. When she stands up her centre of mass
rises, so the effective length l DECREASES.
steps.why: The mass of the girl never appears in T = 2π√(l/g) — only WHERE her mass sits does, and standing moves it up.
common_mistakes: Saying nothing changes because it is the same swing and the same girl.

recall.must_convey: That standing raises her centre of mass, so the effective length of the pendulum decreases.
accept: length is to the centre of mass

steps.label: The frequency changes
lines: For a simple pendulum T = 2π√(l/g), so a
smaller l gives a smaller T. Since n = 1/T,
steps.why: Shorter pendulum, quicker swing — the same reason a short rope swings faster than a long one.
common_mistakes: Concluding the frequency decreases by reading n ∝ √l instead of 1/√l.

recall.must_convey: That T is 2 pi root l by g, so a smaller l means a smaller T and a higher frequency.
accept: n is one by root l
